title: Faridpur hospital holds 1,425 patients a day in 500 beds
excerpt: An upgrade to 1,000 beds was approved in 2023, but no buildings or staff followed. Patients from at least eight districts are treated on floors and verandas.

image.credit: File photo: Ashonko / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
Faridpur Medical College Hospital admits an average of 1,425 inpatients a day, nearly three times its 500 beds, Prothom Alo reported on Tuesday (24 November), citing hospital sources. Many patients are treated on the floor and on ward verandas.

The government approved raising the hospital to 1,000 beds on 11 June 2023, but neither the buildings nor the staff have followed. When it moved from 250 to 500 beds in 2013, the hospital asked for 400 more staff and got 50. Of 67 third-class staff posts, 37 are filled, and of 123 fourth-class posts, 76 are filled. Another 154 people work through outsourcing.

The 32 wards need 10 to 12 ward attendants each but have 31 between them. Relatives often push trolleys themselves, and some fall into the hands of brokers. On Sunday a teenager injured in a motorcycle crash could not get an X-ray because it was after 1pm, and his family had to take him to a private clinic.

Prof Khan Mohammad Arif, head of medicine, said his ward had 700 patients, including dengue cases. "It is not possible to make anyone happy with the care in this situation," he told Prothom Alo.

Why it matters

The hospital serves people from Faridpur, Rajbari, Magura, Jhenaidah, Gopalganj, Madaripur, Shariatpur, Kushtia and nearby districts. Overcrowding of this kind pushes poorer families into private clinics and raises infection risk. It also shows how bed upgrades approved on paper can stall without staff and money.

What to watch

Whether the health ministry includes Faridpur in its plan to fill vacant posts, and whether money for the 1,000-bed building appears in the revised development budget.
